name: Konstantin Nikolaev
current_role: Private investor; owner of La Madonnina winery (Bolgheri, Tuscany); former co-owner of Globaltrans/N-Trans and Global Ports
profile: Russian-born logistics entrepreneur (b. 1971, Dnipropetrovsk) who co-founded Severstaltrans in 1996 with Nikita Mishin, Andrei Filatov and Alexei Mordashov, later N-Trans, which grew into Globaltrans (Russia's largest private rail operator) and Global Ports. He sold out of the ports in 2017 and completed his exit from all Russian business in January 2024; the Tuscan winery is now his main focus.
interesting_fact: He is one of the co-founders of the Moscow School of Management Skolkovo, described as Russia's first business school; he also was an early investor in US-based American Ethane.
deep_cut_fact: He studied philosophy at Moscow State University and wrote his thesis on Plato's Republic, then started his logistics career as a forwarding agent at Murmansk port coordinating ship loading.
notes: Sensitive profile: under Ukrainian sanctions (2023) and has had press coverage tied to US politics; avoid those topics. Citizen of Malta per Wikipedia. No published personal/office contact found; any approach would likely be via the La Madonnina winery or a lawyer/spokesperson.

name: Sergey Kasyanenko
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Management Board, Orimi Group (Russia)
profile: Co-founder of Orimi, Russia's largest producer of tea and roasted coffee (brands Greenfield, TESS, Jardin, Princess Noori). Orimi started in 1994 as Orimi Trade, a wholesaler of flour, sugar and tea, then built its own packaging and coffee plants in Leningrad Region. Most of his fortune is cash from roughly $1.5bn of Orimi dividends.
interesting_fact: He holds a Ph.D. in physics and mathematics before becoming a tea and coffee magnate.
deep_cut_fact: Orimi's very first tea brand, launched at its founding in 1994, was 'Princess Kandy'; within two years Orimi Trade was one of Russia's six biggest tea importers. He and co-founder Alexander Evnevich personally opened Orimi's instant-coffee plant with the Leningrad Region governor.
notes: Very low public profile; little English-language coverage. Company press office is the only published route.

name: Song Weiping
current_role: Founder of Greentown China; controls Bluetown (Lancheng) town-development / construction-management business
profile: Song Weiping (b. 1957, Sheng County, Shaoxing) is a Hangzhou property developer who founded Greentown China with his wife Xia Yibo in 1994, building it into a premium developer in Zhejiang, Shanghai and Beijing. He resigned as Greentown co-chairman in 2019 to focus on Bluetown and 'ideal town' projects.
interesting_fact: He founded the Zhejiang Greentown football club (Hangzhou Greentown F.C.) and is a well-known football fan.
deep_cut_fact: A 1982 history graduate of Hangzhou University, he taught at a party school for five years, then worked as a secretary at a computer company in Zhuhai before returning to Hangzhou and founding Greentown with RMB150,000.
notes: Fortune shared with wife Xia Yibo. Current Bluetown title not confirmed for 2025-26. No personal published contacts; route would be via Greentown China or Bluetown corporate offices.

name: James Cameron
current_role: Filmmaker (Lightstorm Entertainment); director of the Avatar franchise; National Geographic explorer and ocean-exploration advocate
profile: Canadian-born (now also New Zealand citizen, 2025) director of The Terminator, Titanic and the Avatar films, three of the four highest-grossing movies ever; his films have grossed roughly $9-10bn. Much of his wealth comes from Avatar profit participation. He developed his own 3D camera and performance-capture tech, and released Avatar: Fire and Ash in December 2025.
interesting_fact: In 2012 he became the first person to make a solo dive to the bottom of the Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep) in the Deepsea Challenger, a sub he helped develop; he also sold The Terminator script for $1 on condition he could direct it.
deep_cut_fact: After dropping out of Fullerton College he worked as a truck driver and high-school janitor, teaching himself special effects in the USC library; he financed his first short film, Xenogenesis (1978), by borrowing money from a consortium of dentists. A frog species, Pristimantis jamescameroni, is named after him.
notes: Lives in New Zealand. No personal social accounts or published personal contact found; approaches go via Lightstorm Entertainment or his talent agency/publicist. Strong energy/sustainability angle: plant-based food businesses, OceanX adviser, ocean exploration tech.

name: Haruko Mikitani
current_role: Major individual shareholder of Rakuten Group; wife of Rakuten founder/CEO Hiroshi 'Mickey' Mikitani
profile: Haruko Mikitani (三谷晴子 as listed; 三木谷晴子) married Hiroshi Mikitani in 1993. Her wealth comes from a personal stake in Rakuten Group, the Japanese e-commerce, fintech and mobile conglomerate her husband founded in 1997; she has kept an almost entirely private profile.
interesting_fact: She is reported to hold roughly 5% of Rakuten in her own name, separate from her husband's direct stake and his Crimson Group holding vehicle (figures vary by source and date).
notes: Very private; no public role, interviews or accounts found. Early-Rakuten back-office role claimed only by a weak source (prabook), not verified. Any approach would realistically go through Rakuten Group corporate communications or the Mikitani family office (Crimson Group). Alive status not independently confirmed (no reports otherwise).

name: Carl Henry Jr. Lindner
current_role: Co-CEO, American Financial Group (since 2005); chairman of Great American Insurance; CEO and majority owner of FC Cincinnati (profile is for Carl H. Lindner III)
profile: The record mixes two people: founder Carl H. Lindner Jr. (Forbes 1996 list) died in October 2011; the current AFG Co-CEO in SEC insider filings is his son Carl H. Lindner III (b. 1953). Lindner III joined AFG in 1975, has chaired Great American Insurance since 1987 and has been co-CEO with brother S. Craig Lindner since 2005; he co-founded FC Cincinnati in 2015.
interesting_fact: He co-founded FC Cincinnati in 2015 and is its majority owner; he and GM Jeff Berding were jointly named 'Cincinnatian of the Year' in 2016 for the club's record-breaking first season.
deep_cut_fact: He started at American Financial in 1975 straight after a University of Cincinnati business degree, two years after his father bought the company, and in 1989 he and his wife Martha were founding benefactors of Cincinnati Hills Christian Academy.

public_contacts.value: Investor & Media Relations (Diane P. Weidner, VP) via phone 513-369-5713 as listed in AFG press releases; no email published

notes: Identity flag: name field says 'Jr.' but the SEC Co-CEO is Carl H. Lindner III; Carl Jr. died 2011. Lost a son in 2025 - avoid. Corporate IR/media relations is the realistic route; FC Cincinnati front office is an alternative.

name: Mai Michael
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Crown New Materials Technology Co., Ltd. (皇冠新材, SZSE: 001381), Zhongshan, China
profile: Mai Michael, also known as Mai Huiquan (麦惠权), is an Australian citizen based in Zhongshan who runs Crown New Materials, a maker of adhesive tapes and materials supplying BYD, Apple and Tesla. He and his sister, vice chair Mai Huixia, control most of the company, which listed on the Shenzhen main board on 3 Nov 2026, lifting both into billionaire status.
interesting_fact: Crown's November 2026 Shenzhen IPO raised about RMB956m and the shares jumped more than 300% on the first trading day, triggering a trading halt.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into the tape business in 1985, he spent three years teaching at an elementary school in Zhongshan, the city where Crown New Materials is now headquartered.
notes: Newly minted billionaire via Nov 2026 IPO; very little English coverage. IR email and board office are from the official listing announcement. Supplies EV makers (BYD, Tesla) - a possible energy/EV angle.

name: Zhang Kapeng
current_role: Chairman and President, Weixing Group (伟星集团), Linhai, Zhejiang; director of Zhejiang Weixing New Building Materials (002372) and Weixing Co. (002003)
profile: Zhang Kapeng (b. January 1965, Linhai, Taizhou) leads Weixing Group, the controlling shareholder of Zhejiang Weixing New Building Materials (PPR/PE plastic piping) and Weixing Co., a leading Chinese maker of buttons and zippers. He and Zhang Sanyun are the listed actual controllers of Weixing New Materials.
interesting_fact: Weixing Group's businesses span from garment accessories (it is one of China's leading button and zipper makers) to building-materials pipes, property and finance - all run out of the small coastal city of Linhai.
deep_cut_fact: He rose from an ordinary factory worker at Weixing, mentored by the company's first-generation leadership, to become group chairman; he holds the title of senior economist and was honored as a national 'Rural Spark Program leader' (全国农村星火带头人).
notes: Low profile; mostly Chinese-language coverage. Deep-cut source is a brand-directory site (moderate reliability). IR email from Weixing New Materials' 2024 annual report summary (April 2025).

name: Jin Liguo
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Dongguan Yiheda Automation Co., Ltd. (怡合达, SZSE ChiNext: 301029)
profile: Jin Liguo (b. May 1973) founded Yiheda, a Dongguan-based one-stop supplier of standardized factory-automation components (a Chinese counterpart to Japan's Misumi) for non-standard automation equipment makers, including lithium-battery and electronics lines. He has run its predecessor since 1999 and has chaired the company since 2017; it listed on ChiNext in 2021.
interesting_fact: Yiheda's model is to standardize the thousands of small mechanical and electrical parts that custom automation-equipment builders need and sell them through a one-stop catalog, cutting design and procurement time for China's automation industry.
deep_cut_fact: With only a high-school education, he started as a technician at the Xingcheng Bearing Factory (1993-95), then worked as a salesman at a Shenyang aerospace special-equipment plant before taking over as general manager of Shenzhen Yiheda in 1999.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts. Board office (secretary Zhang Meiqi) is the published route. Customers include new-energy/battery equipment makers - relevant energy angle.

name: Dong Mingzhu
current_role: Chairwoman (and president per latest available sources) of Gree Electric Appliances, Zhuhai
profile: Dong Mingzhu (b. 1954, Nanjing) joined Gree's predecessor in 1990 at 36 as an air-conditioner saleswoman and rose to head of sales (1994), president (2001) and chairwoman (2012), making Gree one of the world's largest air-conditioner makers. She pushed Gree into solar, robotics and EVs (acquiring Yinlong in 2016) and is one of China's most famous executives.
interesting_fact: Fortune ranked her among the most powerful women in business internationally; Gree says most of its 44 'internationally leading' technologies relate to green energy, and 2023 was its most profitable year (about $4.1bn).
deep_cut_fact: Sent as a junior saleswoman to Anhui, one of China's poorer provinces, she alone produced about one-eighth of Gree's annual sales, which got her noticed by first GM Zhu Jianghong. Her 2006 memoir 'Regretless Pursuit' was turned into a CCTV television series.
notes: High-profile, outspoken; avoid her 2025 remarks on overseas returnees. Strong energy angle (solar air-conditioning, energy storage, Gree Altairnano/Yinlong EV batteries). Confirm her current president title before outreach.
